 2026 CMA Awards Predictions: Who Will Win?
 Billboard offers predictions on which artists will take home the biggest wins at Wednesday night's CMA Awards.
 By 
 Melinda Newman , Jessica Nicholson 
 11/17/2026

 Ella Langley at the Billboard Women in Music 2026 held at the Hollywood Palladium on April 29, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
 Billboard 
 Will the year of Ella Langley continue at the 60 th annual CMA Awards on Nov. 18? 
 Langley has already had a record-breaking 2026, as her song “Choosin’ Texas” set the all-time mark for the most weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with a total of 27 weeks in the top spot. 
 The tune’s massive success helped Langley earn nine nominations for the awards, leading all artists and tying the record for the most nods in one year by a female artist (matching Miranda Lambert’s 2010 and 2014 hauls and Lainey Wilson’s 2023 tally). 
 Lambert follows Langley with seven nominations; Kacey Musgraves and producer Ben West have five, while Cody Johnson, Chris Stapleton and Stephen Wilson Jr. have four each. Wilson, who will return as host for the third time (and the second as a solo host), earned three nods. 
 The evening, which will air on ABC and stream live on Disney + for the first time from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena, will also include performances by Cody Johnson, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley, Tim McGraw and more.
 The eligibility period for nominated releases runs July 1, 2025-June 30, 2026. Last year’s top winners include Lainey Wilson, Cody Johnson, Ella Langley, Riley Green and Zach Top.
 Here are Billboard ’s predictions on who will emerge victorious in select categories, from Melinda Newman (executive editor, West Coast and country) and Jessica Nicholson (associate editor, Nashville).
 Billboard will be streaming live from the CMA red carpet starting at 6 p.m. ET/ 3 p.m. PT on Samsung TV Plus, Amazon Fire TV, Billboard News YouTube channel and Billboard Country’s X account. 
 Entertainer of the year
 Luke Combs
 Cody Johnson
 Ella Langley
 Chris Stapleton
 Lainey Wilson
 Newman: Wilson, who is the reigning entertainer of the year, first won this award in 2023 as she was rising to superstardom — just as Langley has done this year. Combs had the biggest touring year, including selling out three Wembley Stadium dates on his European tour. Stapleton is still looking for his first win with his 10 th nomination. Johnson took home the award at the ACM Awards and is just growing stronger, so all are worthy (the notable omission here is 2024 winner Wallen). However, even though it feels early for her, the momentum for Langley is too strong. 
 Will win: Ella Langley
 Nicholson: Wilson took home her first CMA Award in 2022 and then earned her first entertainer of the year win just one year later; this marks her fourth nomination in the category (she’s won twice previously). It feels like Langley is on a very similar trajectory, having earned her first win in 2024 and just ascended to headlining arenas on her The Dandelion Tour this year, as “Choosin’ Texas” dominates the Hot 100. Meanwhile, Luke Combs keeps building his global touring footprint, Stapleton remains one of country music’s most consistent touring acts and Johnson keeps flexing his musical muscle with hit songs and engaging headlining shows. Still, this feels like Langley’s year.
 Will win: Ella Langley
 Album of the year
 Award goes to artist, producer(s) and mix engineer(s) 
 Ain’t In It For My Health – Zach Top; Producer: Carson Chamberlain; Mix Engineer: Matt Rovey
 Dandelion – Ella Langley; Producers: Devin Dawson, Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Ben West; Mix Engineer: Dave Clauss
 Middle of Nowhere – Kacey Musgraves; Producers: Ian Fitchuk, Luke Laird, Kacey Musgraves, Daniel Tashian; Mix Engineers: Serban Ghenea, Konrad Snyder
 Parker McCollum – Parker McCollum; Producers: Frank Liddell, Eric Masse; Mix Engineer: Eric Masse
 The Way I Am – Luke Combs; Producers: Luke Combs, Chip Matthews, Jonathan Singleton; Mix Engineer: Chip Matthews
 Newman: All five entries in this extremely competitive category could easily and deservedly walk away with the award. Top and Langley are the relative newcomers who have taken country music by storm. Musgraves is a perennial nominee who has only had one of her six studio albums not nominated for album of the year. McCollum’s self-titled set won at the ACMs and Combs is always a contender. But it just feels like it’s Langley’s year.
 Will win: Dandelion 
 Nicholson: Luke Combs, who previously won in this category for his Growin’ Up , turned in another solid album this year, as did McCollum and Top. Meanwhile, Musgraves’s Middle of Nowhere marked one of her most creatively adventurous albums yet, and she previously won in this category for Golden Hour . Beyond “Choosin’ Texas,” Langley’s Dandelion notched hits including “Loving Life Again” and “Butterfly Season” that have had an enduring connection with fans. Look for Langley to continue sweeping up wins this year, taking home the trophy here.
 Will win: Dandelion 
 Single of the year
 Award goes to the artist, producer(s) and mix engineer(s) 
 “Be Her” – Ella Langley; Producers: Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley, Ben West; Mix Engineer: Dave Clauss
 “Choosin’ Texas” – Ella Langley; Producers: Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley, Ben West; Mix Engineer: Dave Clauss
 “I Knew It, I Knew You” – Taylor Swift; Producers: Jack Antonoff, Taylor Swift; Mix Engineer: Laura Sisk
 “Somewhere Over Laredo” – Lainey Wilson; Producer: Jay Joyce; Mix Engineers: Jason Hall, Jay Joyce
 “The Fall” – Cody Johnson; Producer: Trent Willmon; Mix Engineer: Jack Clarke
 Newman: There’s a very slim chance that Langley could split the vote between her two songs and Swift could swoop in to win her first single of the year award at the CMAs (unbelievably, she hasn’t won it before) — but who are we kidding? In an evening with some very tough races that are hard to call, this one is the easiest. This is no disrespect for any of the other songs here, that in any other year could all easily win, but “Choosin’ Texas” already has this sewn up. (It will be interesting to see if Swift loses here, then goes on to win the Oscar for her song from Toy Story 5 .)
 Will win: “Choosin’ Texas”
 Nicholson: With “Choosin’ Texas” dominating the Hot 100 this year, and “Be Her” also connecting with fans, Langley has a strong shot at taking home the prize here, though Swift also has her first nomination in this category since 2013. Wilson and Johnson have also earned chart hits with their entries, but it feels like this category will find Langley in the winner’s circle. This would also be a repeat win for Ella, who won in this category last year with “You Look Like You Love Me,” her collab with Riley Green.
 Will win: “Choosin’ Texas”
 Song of the year
 Award goes to songwriter(s) 
 “Be Her”; Songwriters: Smith Ahnquist, Michael Hardy, Ella Langley, Jordan Schmidt
 “Beautiful Things”; Songwriters: Jessi Alexander, Jessie Jo Dillon, Connie Harrington, Megan Moroney
 “Choosin’ Texas”; Songwriters: Luke Dick, Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Joybeth Taylor
 “Dry Spell”; Songwriters: Luke Laird, Shane McAnally, Kacey Musgraves, Josh Osborne
 “Gary”; Songwriter: Stephen Wilson Jr.
 Newman: We could sing the praises of the other songs here, all of which have their strong points, especially Musgraves’ humorous “Dry Spell” and Wilson’s poignant “Gary” — but, like single of the year, Langley and her co-writers are taking home this award.
 Will win: “Choosin’ Texas”
 Nicholson: The song of the year category typically focuses more on songcraft rather than commercial success, and each of these final nominees certainly have superb artistic merits, but look for Langley and her co-writers to continue the winning streak here and making it a repeat win for Langley in this category.
 Will win: “Choosin’ Texas”
 Female vocalist of the year
 Miranda Lambert
 Ella Langley
 Megan Moroney
 Kacey Musgraves
 Lainey Wilson
 Newman: Lambert has won a record seven times (and been nominated 19 times—also a record) but hasn’t won since 2017. Wilson has had a lock on the category, winning four consecutive times starting in 2022, while Musgraves won once in 2018. All the contenders had great years — but, once again, 2026 is Langley’s year. 
 Will win: Ella Langley
 Nicholson: Each artist here has had a year filled with career highs and milestones, including Moroney earning her first Billboard 200 chart-topper with Cloud 9 , Lambert not only releasing acclaimed songs like the Stapleton collab “A Song to Sing” but also co-writing and co-producing “Choosin’ Texas,” while Wilson has continued her own winning streak with “Phone, Keys, Wallet.” Musgraves has been headlining shows and issued the creative and thoughtful Middle of Nowhere . But With Langley earning multiple smash hits this year and leading her headlining arena tour, she seems to have this win in the bag.
 Will win: Ella Langley
 Male vocalist of the year
 Luke Combs
 Cody Johnson
 Chris Stapleton
 Zach Top
 Stephen Wilson Jr.
 Newman:  This is a tough category, with Morgan Wallen left out after being nominated the past four years, and hot acts like Riley Green and Parker McCollum also not nominated. But that just goes to show how competitive it is for male artists right now, and how many strong singers there are out there. Johnson, Combs and Stapleton have all won before, and it feels like it’s neo-traditionalist Zach Top’s turn. 
 Will win: Zach Top
 Nicholson: Chris Stapleton and Luke Combs are always top contenders in this category, while Johnson keeps doubling down on top-crafted hits like “The Fall.” Zach Top continued spearheading his headlining tour and bringing superb ‘90s-flavored country, while Stephen Wilson Jr. continues gaining fans and strong industry support with his vulnerable songwriting and rock-infused sound. Still, look for Johnson to repeat last year’s win in this category.
 Will win: Cody Johnson
 Vocal group of the year
 Lady A
 Little Big Town
 Midland
 Old Dominion
 The Red Clay Strays
 Newman: As usual with this category, the CMA voters played it safe going with veteran, mainstream groups (other than last year’s winners The Red Clay Strays), instead of adding in some of the newer country-leaning bands who are filling venues right now (even if country radio still largely ignores them) like Treaty Oak Revival and Flatland Calvary. This is Little Big Town’s 21st consecutive nomination! That’s not to say that that the older acts aren’t worthy contenders, it would just be nice for the category to look like 2026 instead of 2018. The older acts will split the votes, and the Red Clay Strays take home the group’s second consecutive win.
 Will win: The Red Clay Strays
 Nicholson: The Red Clay Strays broke Old Dominion’s winning streak in this category last year, picking up their the group’s win in the category. The Strays also represent the only newer act of the bunch in a category that is stacked with past winners and nominees (LBT has taken home the win six times, Lady A three times, Old Dominion seven times, while Midland has earned seven nominations in the category). With 2026’s Gratitude , The Red Clay Strays seem to be picking up even more steam.
 Will win: The Red Clay Strays
 Vocal duo of the year
 Brooks & Dunn
 Brothers Osborne
 Dan + Shay
 Muscadine Bloodline
 Thelma & James
 Newman: For the last several years, the CMAs have struggled to round out this category, especially since Florida Georgia Line went on hiatus (now that they’re back together, expect to see them here again next year). This is perpetually a race between Brooks & Dunn, Brothers Osborne and Dan + Shay — and now that Maddie & Tae have broken up, the voters must figure out a way to round it out. Muscadine Bloodline is very strong, with Thelma & James slowly gaining ground, but Brooks & Dunn is taking home the trophy. The duo will extend its record for the most CMA Awards wins by any artist at 21. 
 Will win: Brooks & Dunn
 Nicholson: Brooks & Dunn, Brothers Osborne and Dan + Shay locked down the winners circle in this category since 2016, though newcomers Muscadine Bloodline has built a strong fanbase and Thelma & James makes a strong debut in the category this year. Brooks & Dunn has been on tour with Morgan Wallen this year, while Brothers Osborne remained in the spotlight with a new album.
 Will win: Brothers Osborne
 Musical event of the year
 Award goes to artists and producer(s) 
 “A Song to Sing” – Miranda Lambert (with Chris Stapleton); Producer: Dave Cobb
 “Horses and Divorces” – Kacey Musgraves (feat. Miranda Lambert); Producers: Kacey Musgraves, Daniel Tashian
 “I Can’t Love You Anymore” – Ella Langley & Morgan Wallen; Producers: Austin Goodloe, Ella Langley, Ben West
 “If I Don’t Leave I’m Gonna Stay” – Carly Pearce & Riley Green; Producers: Carly Pearce, Ben West
 “McArthur” – HARDY, Eric Church, Morgan Wallen & Tim McGraw; Producer: Jay Joyce
 Newman: This is the only category where Morgan Wallen received any nominations, and he’s competing against himself here. Green’s and Pearce’s song would have probably stood a better chance in music video of the year, given the steaminess of the clip, but it’s only nod is in this category. Musgraves and Lambert buried the hatchet with this song, but Lambert will likely split the vote with her Stapleton duet here. “McArthur” was an event record with a true constellation of stars, even though it stalled at No. 17 on Billboard ’s Country Airplay chart.
 Will win: “McArthur”
 Nicholson: The Langley/Wallen collab on “I Can’t Love You Anymore” was a hit this year on the radio-driven Country Airplay chart and all-genre Hot 100, while Lambert’s collab with Stapleton earned multiple Grammy nominations last year. Meanwhile, “McArthur” is the most star-studded of the bunch, which could tip it into the winner’s circle — but it is also likely that the win could go to “A Song To Sing,” given CMA voters’ love for both Lambert and Stapleton.
 Will win: “A Song to Sing”
 Music video of the year
 Award goes to artist(s) and director(s) 
 “Choosin’ Texas” – Ella Langley; Directors: Ella Langley, Caylee Robillard, Wales Toney
 “Dry Spell” – Kacey Musgraves; Directors: Hannah Lux Davis, Kacey Musgraves
 “Gary” – Stephen Wilson Jr.; Directors: Tim Cofield, Stephen Wilson Jr.
 “The Fall” – Cody Johnson; Director: Dustin Haney
 “White Horse” – Chris Stapleton; Director: Running Bear
 Newman:  Like music event, this is one of the few categories where it feels like Langley might not be a shoo-in. The video for “Choosin’ Texas” is a fun mini movie, but has stiff competition from all the entries, including Musgraves’ funny, suggestive clip; Wilson’s moving story video and both Johnson’s video with real bullfighter Cody Webster and Stapleton’s high-concept video starring his buddy Josh Brolin (blink and you’ll miss Stapleton in the clip). 
 Will win: “Dry Spell”
 Nicholson: This year’s nominated clips run the gamut from star-studded affairs such as Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” to Musgraves’ comedic “Dry Spell.” Still, Wilson Jr. seems to have been a country voter favorite of late, so the win could go to his and Cofield’s dramatic clip for “Gary.”
 Will win: “Gary”
 New artist of the year
 Avery Anna
 Carter Faith
 Emily Ann Roberts
 Tucker Wetmore
 Stephen Wilson Jr.
 Newman: Wetmore — who, along with Wilson repeats being nominated here — is the only chart topper in a field that is mainly dominated by critical favorites. It’s a strong slate, full of artists who have much promise. Anna took home new female at the ACMs in May, while Wetmore won new male. Wilson is an industry darling so he’s also a leading contender, but Wetmore has made the biggest commercial strides. 
 Will win: Tucker Wetmore
 Nicholson: Each of these artists has had a breakthrough year in distinct ways. Wetmore has gained significant momentum on country radio and streaming, earning his first Country Airplay chart-topper with “Brunette,” adding to two previous Country Airplay top 5 hits. With her debut album Cherry Valley and a role in the new film Heartland , Carter Faith has established herself as a multi-platform artist. Meanwhile, Emily Ann Roberts has cemented herself as a traditional country torchbearer while also forging a multi-faceted brand as both musician and social media personality, Avery Anna’s lean into her rock influences has helped her stand out, and Wilson Jr has become a favorite performer at country awards shows. Still, Wetmore seems to have had the most high-profile success of the current crop of nominees.
 Will win: Tucker Wetmore
